findings.finding: SoFi is a bank holding company whose profit is net interest income on a fast-growing fair-value loan book funded by member deposits (deposits $51.3bn, 90% of average liabilities, 1.45pp cheaper than warehouse funding), plus fee revenue from the Loan Platform Business, Financial Services and the Technology Platform (fee share 42%). Value is set by return on equity against the cost of equity, so the residual-income lens applies, not an operating DCF.

Growth is structural share gain, not cycle: members +36% to 17.1m, products +44% to 26.7m, originations +71% to $16.9bn, adjusted net revenue +44% in Q3 2026. The macro tailwind is limited (2026 guidance assumed two cuts and got a hike, yet was raised). The open residual in the econ review is the deposit funding benefit (13.5% not explained by deposits x cost advantage).

Retail consumers borrow (personal loans $30.9bn UPB, student $18.1bn, home $1.8bn) with no customer concentration; third-party loan buyers fund the Loan Platform Business ($3.8bn originated for them in Q3). LPB revenue fell from its Q4 2025 peak (153.4m in Q3 2026 vs 167.9m a year earlier), so the capital-light fee channel is shrinking while on-balance-sheet lending grows.

Computed high_growth / fast_grower is confirmed for the franchise (revenue +44%), but the valuation lens is a growing bank: returns on equity (ROE about 8.6% annualised, ROTE about 10% in Q3 2026; FY2025 ROE 5.7%) are below the cost of equity today, so the value hinges on the ROE path, not on revenue growth alone.

Beat-and-raise record on revenue and EBITDA: actual / guided midpoint 1.08 (Q2 2025 revenue), 1.11 (FY2025 revenue), 1.23 (FY2025 EBITDA), 1.05 (Q1 2026 revenue), 1.08 (Q2 2026 revenue); FY2026 revenue guide raised from 4.655bn to 5.04bn. But net income conversion is weak: FY2026 EPS guide moved only 0.60 to 0.61 and net income 825m to 840m as the extra revenue went to marketing and rates. Revenue guidance is a floor; earnings guidance is close to delivery.

Management guides FY2027 to about $6.4bn adjusted net revenue (+27%), $2.24bn adjusted EBITDA (35%), $1.28bn net income (20% margin) and EPS 0.90, with a 2025-2028 revenue CAGR of at least 30% and EPS CAGR 38-42%. On a book of about $12.4bn average in 2027 that is an ROE of about 10% (computed), below the cost of equity; guidance, not fact.

All major loans are carried at fair value, so credit and rates hit revenue through marks, not provision (Q3 provision only $14.7m). The cumulative fair-value premium fell to about 3.3% of personal-loan UPB and 1.9% of student-loan UPB in Q3 2026 (about $1.4bn, about 14% of tangible book) as benchmark rates rose 76-90bp; the personal-loan default assumption rose to 5.10% from 4.77%. A +100bp parallel move lowers the fair value of rate-sensitive assets by $1,040.8m before hedges (June 2026).

Reported personal-loan NCO 2.26% is flattered by late-stage delinquent loan sales; the all-in rate excluding those sales is about 3.4% (down from about 4.4%). Student NCO 0.63%; credit card NCO 7.77% on a small book. Credit improved, but the reported figure understates loss content.

CET1 fell from 22.8% (Dec 2025) to 18.7% (June 2026) and 16.9% (Sep 2026) as risk-weighted assets grew from $37.2bn to $48.7bn to $56.2bn (+68% y/y); requirement 7.0% incl. buffer. Shares outstanding rose about 18% since Dec 2024 through two raises (about $3.2bn net at $20.85 and $27.50) plus SBC (about $290m a year, expensed in GAAP net income). The Federal Reserve dividend policy leaves no funds free for dividends (June 2026): payout is zero, growth is funded by retained profit or new equity.

Technology Platform revenue fell 24% y/y to $87.4m with contribution margin down to 16% from 28%; Financial Services revenue grew 25% while products grew 44% (revenue per product $90, down from $104); sales and marketing about +55% y/y. Lending carries 62% of contribution profit.

flags: Piotroski 2/6 (mixed-weak; developed on value stocks, partly uninformative for a fast-growing bank): carried to the bear
ROE (8.6% annualised Q3 2026, 5.7% FY2025) below the cost of equity: value creation not yet shown
Fair-value premium shrinking (PL 4.68% to 3.31% of UPB in one quarter) and default assumption rising three quarters in a row
Rate sensitivity: +100bp = -$1.04bn fair value before hedges (about 9% of book); liability-sensitive NII (-$159m)
CET1 down about 2pp per quarter; RWA +68% y/y: growth may need new equity or slower balance-sheet growth
Dilution: shares +18% since Dec 2024; SBC about $290m a year; 2029 convertible $862.5m
Reported personal-loan NCO 2.26% vs about 3.4% all-in (delinquent loan sales)
Loan Platform Business and Technology Platform revenue declining; FS revenue per product down 13%
Net income guidance barely moved while revenue guidance rose $385m (low conversion)
SEC companyfacts 'revenue' tag (FY2025 619m) is not total net revenue (3.61bn): structured revenue history is unusable for a bank; growth drivers use the releases

economics.reason: Revenue growth comes from member, product and deposit share gains (members +36%, deposits +37% y/y) and was raised through an adverse rate year; consumer-credit cyclicality is real but enters through the ROE path (fair-value marks, charge-offs) in the bear, not as a revenue cycle peak.

type.override_reason: Type kept; the valuation lens is the bank residual-income model (ROE vs cost of equity), because SoFi is a bank holding company whose balance sheet is the product.
